title: Relevance Meets Diversity: A User-Centric Framework for Knowledge Exploration Through Recommendations

problem.claim: Recommendation systems must balance relevance and diversity, which typically trade off against each other and can reduce user engagement when diversity is increased.

gap.claim: Existing approaches combine relevance and diversity into a single objective for a fixed recommendation list size but do not model user interaction with recommended items.

contributions.claim: A user-centric framework is developed around the interplay among relevance, diversity, and user behavior, with diversity used as a surrogate for the amount of knowledge obtained.
A probabilistic user-behavior model is proposed in which users continue interacting while recommendations remain relevant but may stop when relevance drops.
A recommendation strategy is proposed that combines relevance and diversity using a copula function.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the copula-based recommendation strategy as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report an extensive evaluation across multiple datasets.
The authors report that their strategy outperforms several state-of-the-art competitors.

narrative_sequence.summary: Relevance and diversity are important recommendation objectives but are in fundamental tension.
Existing methods optimize a combined relevance-diversity objective without accounting for user interaction.
The paper centers user behavior and targets the total knowledge encountered rather than engagement alone.
The paper models relevance-dependent stopping behavior and proposes a copula-based strategy combining relevance and diversity.
The authors report multi-dataset evaluation, improved performance over several state-of-the-art competitors, and public implementation availability.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not detail the probabilistic model or copula-based optimization procedure.
The abstract does not identify the amount of knowledge measure beyond using diversity as a surrogate.
